user: What different forms of information do I need from my cloned repositories in order to set up my application?
assistant: It appears that you will need access to the code and any associated submodules within your cloned repositories to set up your application. By default, the Git clone in the pipelines does not clone the submodules in a repository. However, you can enable cloning the submodules in the user repositories by setting the opt-in flag `opt-in-clone-submodules` to 1. The `.gitmodules` file in the Git repository must use either HTTPS URLs or relative URLs for the submodules to be cloned. Additionally, you may need to configure any necessary dependencies, build instructions, and deployment scripts, which are typically found in a README file or a similar documentation within the repository.
user: how to configure
assistant: To configure cloning of Git submodules, you can follow these steps:
1. Enable cloning of the submodules by setting the opt-in flag `opt-in-clone-submodules` to  1 to enable cloning of the submodules
2. Set the opt-in flag opt-in-clone-submodules-with-remote to 1 to enable cloning of the submodules by using the status of the submodule’s remote-tracking branch to update the submodule, rather than the superproject’s recorded SHA-1.
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
I meant how to configure dependencies, build instructions, and deployment script
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
I apologize for the confusion. To configure dependencies, build instructions, and deployment scripts, you should check the README file or any documentation provided in the repository. These details can vary depending on the specific project and its requirements. Here are some general steps you can follow:

1. Install the dependencies listed in the requirements.txt file to be able to run the app locally.
2. Run the build script.  Go into the root of the project and type the following: ./build.sh.  You can run this script to compile the source code and prepare it for deployment.

If you cannot find the necessary information in the provided documents, you might need to consult the project's maintainers or community for assistance.

Go into the root of the project and type the following:

./build.sh





 Step 5: Watch your trucks truckin' 

The end of the script will output a URL — something like https:// some.thing.eu-gb.appdomain.cloud.

If you visit the URL that has been generated, you should be able to see a map of the US and, after a few seconds, several markers on the map that represent your trucks:

Zoom
